identity: Neutral trans-HONO nitrous acid, planar singlet ground state, CAS 7782-77-6 with exact ATcT suffix ``*1``. JANAF provides separate cis and trans tables and the runtime has separate species. NASA HNO2 explicitly describes a cis-trans mixture; matching only the elemental formula would combine different thermodynamic species.
recommendation: Retain the current trans-HONO fit for this source-review stage. Its energy difference is small and the available NASA function is a mixture; consider trans as the shared reference in a later joint cis/trans assessment.
science: The original JANAF trans evaluation page 1289 was visually inspected and explicitly describes a single conformer, with symmetry number one and its own frequencies. Current/JANAF differs by less than 1.46% at all four hot nodes. The same-isomer ATcT-minus-JANAF atomization-energy shift is +0.185 kJ/mol, giving K ratios 1.01494-1.00558 over 1500-4000 K. No NASA native or energy-aligned ratio is reported for this individual conformer.
modern: The 2025 TIPS paper explicitly sums cis and trans, uses nuclear-spin factor six, and adopts the 2023 measured ground-level gap 95.8 +/- 9.2 cm-1. This is a ground-state energy difference, not a torsional barrier despite the 2023 title. Rounded ATcT 1.228 conformer values imply 1.610 kJ/mol (about 134.6 cm-1), while old JANAF implies 2.165 kJ/mol; the inspected leading ATcT cis contributors list older measurements. These alternatives deserve a joint energy assessment, not an undocumented direct replacement by the newest number. The 2025 spectroscopy paper improves selected interacting bands but does not establish a complete hot partition function for an individual conformer. The pinned gap replay converts the 2023 result to 1.14602 +/- 0.11006 kJ/mol. At a fixed trans reference it would raise cis K relative to the rounded ATcT-gap model by only 3.79% at 1500 K and 1.40% at 4000 K; this sensitivity is not an adopted correction.
importance: HONO is a reactive atmospheric nitrogen species and an OH photochemical source. The present hot hydrogen-rich equilibrium inventory is tiny and does not test cooler oxidizing atmospheres or photochemistry.
conventions: Each curated isomer is a separate chemical species. A summed cis/trans partition function contains the relative ground-state Boltzmann weight and must never be copied into both rows or treated as a constant conformer multiplier. The NASA mixed function is pinned only to prove the identity mismatch; its standalone molecular G/H/S/Cp are explicitly segregated from valid single-isomer comparisons.
followup: For a joint candidate, choose one trans energy reference, compare the measured 2023 conformer gap with the ATcT covariance/provenance and retain separate isomer thermal functions. Test both individual changes and the combined HONO inventory. The 2023 full text, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2023.108727, would sharpen the energy assessment; the inspected 2025 primary paper already reproduces its key number. Its absence is not a hold on this identity/source review.
